title: Maximum Number of Ways to Partition an Array
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n, determine the maximum number of ways to partition the array by changing at most one element to k.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n, determine the maximum number of ways to partition the array by changing at most one element to k. A partition is valid if the sum of elements before the pivot equals the sum of elements after the pivot, with 1 <= pivot < n.
constraints: nums has 2 through 100000 integers and k is an integer in the same bounded range.
A pivot splits before index p, 1<=p<n, and is valid when left and right sums match.
Change at most one nums element to k and maximize the number of valid pivots.
reference_solution:
def maximum_partition_ways(nums,k):
    total=sum(nums);prefix=0;right=Counter()
    for value in nums[:-1]:prefix+=value;right[2*prefix-total]+=1
    answer=right[0];left=Counter();prefix=0
    for index,value in enumerate(nums):
        delta=k-value
        answer=max(answer,left[delta]+right[-delta])
        prefix+=value
        if index<len(nums)-1:
            difference=2*prefix-total;right[difference]-=1;left[difference]+=1
    return answer

hints: Represent each pivot by difference 2*prefix-total; changing a value shifts that difference with opposite signs depending on which side contains it.
Sweep the changed index with counters for pivots to its left and right.
For delta=k-nums[i], candidate=left[delta]+right[-delta]; then move the next pivot difference from right to left.
Left pivots place the changed element on their right and need old difference delta; right pivots place it on their left and need old difference -delta.
